task.description: Implement the gate-approved design at lib/letflow/design/iss0732-promotion-apply-assertion-gate.md exactly as specified (it is CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-passed; do not deviate from its error-reason names, with-chain ordering, or gate condition without flagging why in your result). This is backend-only for this run (frontend NonSkippableApprovalGate.tsx is out of scope, tracked as ISS-0767). Implement: the new precondition in Letflow.Definitions.Promotion.apply_review/4's `with` chain (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex), the new apply_review_error() union members, and the corresponding new render_apply/2 (or equivalent) clauses in lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex mapping each new error reason to its documented HTTP response. Run the existing test suite for the affected modules (at minimum test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and test/letflow/routers/promotions_test.exs) and the full suite before completing -- quote real mix test output, never a prediction. Do not weaken or remove the EXISTING R8 assertions_failed == 0 gate condition or verify_apply_digest/2's constant-time comparison while making this change.
acceptance_criteria: apply_review/4 rejects an Apply with no PromotionAssertionRun for the review (returns the design's :assertion_run_missing reason, nothing written)
apply_review/4 rejects an Apply whose latest assertion run's plan_digest does not match the digest being applied (returns :assertion_run_digest_mismatch, nothing written)
apply_review/4 rejects an Apply whose latest matching-digest assertion run has assertions_failed > 0 (returns :assertion_run_failed, nothing written)
apply_review/4 still succeeds when a matching-digest, assertions_failed == 0 run exists (no regression to the existing happy path)
R7 router (lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex handle_apply/2 path) returns the design-specified HTTP response for each new error reason
mix test output is quoted verbatim in result.summary, full suite, 0 regressions vs. main

result.summary:
Implemented the gate-approved design exactly: added private verify_rehearsed/2 to lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex's apply_review/4 with-chain (inserted after verify_approved/1, before do_apply_review/3), 3 new apply_review_error() union members (:assertion_run_missing, :assertion_run_digest_mismatch, :assertion_run_failed), and 3 new render_apply/2 clauses in lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex (each Response.conflict/2, 409, with its own design-specified detail string). Existing R8 assertions_failed==0 gate condition and verify_apply_digest/2's constant-time comparison untouched.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, 0 warnings/errors.

Targeted suite (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs + test/letflow/routers/promotions_test.exs + test/letflow/routers/req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs, 54 tests total via a single run):
  Finished in 60.1 seconds (0.00s async, 60.1s sync)
  Result: 54 passed
0 failures.

Implementing verify_rehearsed/2 broke 3 pre-existing tests in test/letflow/routers/req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs (AC1 R7 happy-path apply, and both AC4 already-applied fixtures) because those fixtures called apply after approve without ever recording a rehearsal -- correctly started 409'ing under the new gate. Fixed by adding an `insert_passing_assertion_run!/3` test helper (directly inserts a matching-digest, status: :passed, assertions_failed: 0 PromotionAssertionRun row, bypassing the real R8 HTTP/SandboxPool round trip that AC1's own R8 describe block already exercises) and calling it at the 3 affected call sites before apply. No assertions in those tests were weakened -- each still checks its original, unrelated behaviour (self-approval-gate ordering, 409-on-already-applied invariance, R7 happy path).

Full mix test, run twice:
  Run A (before the req077 test-fixture fix): 'Finished in 2169.1 seconds (17.6s async, 2151.5s sync)' / 'Result: 4490/4495 passed (6/6 properties, 4484/4489 tests), 23 excluded' / 'Failed: 5 tests' -- all 5 were: 3x the req077 fixture-gap tests just fixed above, plus 2x Letflow.IdentityTest resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and resolve_realm_by_tenant/1 (REQ-019 AC1) -- confirmed via `git stash` against this same branch unmodified: those 2 fail there too (52/54 on test/letflow/identity_test.exs alone), i.e. pre-existing, already tracked as ISS-0766 per ORCH (flaky under shared non-partitioned DB state), not caused by this change.
  Run B (after the fix, full suite): 'Finished in 2805.3 seconds (22.4s async, 2782.8s sync)' / 'Result: 4487/4495 passed (6/6 properties, 4481/4489 tests), 23 excluded' / 'Failed: 8 tests' -- the 2 ISS-0766 IdentityTest failures again, PLUS 6 new failures, all in Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest/Letflow.ServiceCatalogReaperTest. Diagnosed, not assumed: each of those 6 failures' own log line reads verbatim 'TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2: deferring this sweep entirely -- another mix test invocation (application_name != ...) is currently connected to this database ... (ISS-0110)' / the equivalent ISS-0414 line for the service-catalog sweep -- i.e. the module's own documented concurrency guard detected a second live `mix test` connection and correctly deferred, which reads as a failed assertion under this suite's fixed test IDs. Confirmed environmental, not code fallout: (a) `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='erl.exe'"` during Run B showed 2 concurrent plain `mix test` processes (no --no-color) that were not mine (I ran only --no-color invocations) -- almost certainly a sibling Claude session/agent in this same repo per this session's own sibling-session guidance; (b) re-ran `mix test test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs` standalone afterward and it reproduced the identical 3/6-passed failure with the identical ISS-0110 deferral log line while those sibling erl.exe processes were still present -- deterministic reproduction of the stated cause, not a guess. Did not kill those processes (not mine to kill; sibling-session discretion favors not disrupting another agent's in-flight run). No full run without sibling interference was captured before completing this handoff, given the ~35-45 min full-suite cost and the already-conclusive standalone reproduction; RELEASE-VALIDATOR or a later full-suite run once sibling sessions are idle should show 4489/4495 (only the 2 known ISS-0766 failures) if this diagnosis holds -- flagged in issues/next_action below rather than asserted as fact.

Did not touch verify_apply_digest/2's constant-time comparison or the existing R8 assertions_failed==0 gate condition anywhere.
